en.greeting: Hi! Today you're the bridge between cultures: you'll explain how people tend to behave and why, choose between direct and indirect politeness for each listener, and make sure nobody hears a polite 'we'll consider it' as a firm yes.

steps.title: Explaining a norm
steps.text: At C1 you explained concepts like sungkan, gotong royong, musyawarah and jam karet in four parts. Now you explain norms, in both directions.
steps.body: A **norm** is an unwritten rule about behaviour: how you address your boss, when you give criticism, what you ask a new colleague. Explain it in four moves: the **tendency** (*In many Indonesian offices…*), the **reason** (respect, harmony, closeness, efficiency), **what it doesn't mean** (*It isn't rudeness*) and **what to do** (*So it's a good idea to…*). Use **many / often / tend to**, never **always / all**, and never say one culture is better.

pairs.en: In many Indonesian offices, …
pairs.id: Di banyak kantor di Indonesia, … (kecenderungan)

pairs.en: People often … / It's common to …
pairs.id: Orang sering … / Biasanya … (kecenderungan)

pairs.en: In some workplaces, …
pairs.id: Di sebagian tempat kerja, … (tidak semua)

pairs.en: It's a way of showing …
pairs.id: Itu cara menunjukkan … (alasannya)

pairs.en: It isn't rudeness. / It isn't personal.
pairs.id: Itu bukan kasar. / Itu bukan soal pribadi. (apa yang bukan)

pairs.en: So it's a good idea to …
pairs.id: Jadi sebaiknya … (apa yang dilakukan)

steps.title: Norms, in both directions
steps.text: Some Indonesian norms explained for foreign colleagues, and some foreign norms explained for Indonesian colleagues.
steps.body: Notice the facts: Indonesians use **Pak / Bu + first name** because many have no family name; many Muslim colleagues fast from dawn to sunset in Ramadan; gifts are often opened later in Indonesia and Japan; and give or receive with the **right hand**.

examples.en: You can call him Pak Budi. Budi is his first name, and many Indonesians don't have a family name.
examples.id: Kamu bisa memanggilnya Pak Budi. Budi itu nama depannya, dan banyak orang Indonesia tidak punya nama keluarga.

examples.en: In Australia it's common to call even the CEO by her first name.
examples.id: Di Australia, memanggil CEO dengan nama depannya saja itu biasa.

examples.en: In many Dutch workplaces, a deadline is a promise, so warn Anna early if it might slip.
examples.id: Di banyak tempat kerja di Belanda, tenggat itu janji, jadi beri tahu Anna dari awal kalau mungkin meleset.

examples.en: Many people here will ask if you're married. It's friendly interest, not nosiness.
examples.id: Banyak orang di sini akan bertanya apakah kamu sudah menikah. Itu bentuk perhatian, bukan ingin tahu urusan orang.

examples.en: Mr Sato may not open your gift in front of you. It's polite, not a sign he doesn't like it.
examples.id: Pak Sato mungkin tidak membuka hadiahmu di depanmu. Itu sopan, bukan tanda ia tidak suka.

steps.title: Your turn: explain a norm
steps.text: An Australian NGO in Lombok. Choose the explanation a good mediator would give.

question.prompt: Kate, the new Australian director of an NGO in Lombok, asks why half the team leave the Friday workshop at 11.30 and come back after 1 p.m. Which explanation is best?
options: Friday is a half day in Indonesia, so they're going home early.
Many Muslim men go to the mosque for Friday prayers around midday, so many workplaces here take a longer break. Lombok is mostly Muslim, so finish the morning session by 11.30.
People here aren't very serious about work on Fridays, so don't plan anything important.
question.explanation: The second answer gives the tendency (**many** workplaces), the reason (Friday prayers) and what to do (finish by 11.30). The first is wrong on the facts: they come back after 1, so they aren't going home. The third turns a religious practice into a stereotype about laziness.

steps.title: Direct and indirect politeness
steps.text: Two simple ideas explain a lot of cross-cultural confusion.
steps.body: **Low-context** (konteks rendah): the message is mostly in the words. **High-context** (konteks tinggi): much of it is in the relationship and what isn't said. Broad tendencies: Dutch, German and Australian speakers more direct; Japanese, Thai and Indonesian speakers more indirect. **Positive politeness** = showing closeness; **negative politeness** = not imposing (*negative* isn't bad). Choose for the listener, the relationship, public or private, and the stakes: **adapt the form, keep the content clear**.

pairs.en: low-context
pairs.id: konteks rendah: pesannya ada di kata-kata

pairs.en: high-context
pairs.id: konteks tinggi: banyak pesan ada di situasi dan yang tidak diucapkan

pairs.en: Great work, everyone! Let's make it even better.
pairs.id: Kerja bagus, semuanya! Ayo buat lebih baik lagi. (kesopanan positif: keakraban)

pairs.en: Sorry to bother you, but could you possibly …?
pairs.id: Maaf mengganggu, tapi apakah Anda bisa …? (kesopanan negatif: tidak memaksakan)

pairs.en: The report needs more data before Friday.
pairs.id: Laporannya butuh data tambahan sebelum Jumat. (langsung)

pairs.en: The figures for Bandung look a little thin.
pairs.id: Angka untuk Bandung kelihatannya agak tipis. (kode halus: tambah datanya)

steps.title: Your turn: choose for the listener
steps.text: A Japanese client and bad news about a delivery. Form and content both matter.

question.prompt: Mr Sato, a senior client from Japan, is visiting the factory in Cikarang. You must tell him that the first shipment will arrive five days late. Which message fits him best?
options: Mr Sato, the shipment is late. It'll arrive on 20 March. That's all we can do.
We will do our best to send it soon, Mr Sato. Please don't worry.
Mr Sato, I'm very sorry. Because one machine broke down, the first shipment will arrive on 20 March, five days late. We've added a night shift so the next shipments stay on schedule.
question.explanation: The third message adapts the **form** for a senior client from a high-context culture (an apology, a reason, a plan) and keeps the **content** clear (the date, five days late). The first is clear but blunt, with no apology. The second is polite but hides the delay: a costly misunderstanding.

steps.title: Bridging meaning: decode, then check
steps.text: Now the most expensive misunderstanding in this lesson.
steps.body: A polite **Iya, nanti kami pertimbangkan** is not a firm yes: *iya* often means *I hear you*, and *we'll consider it* may be a **soft no** (the same goes for *kami usahakan* and *agak sulit, Pak*). Don't translate it word for word, and don't turn every iya into a no. **Interpret with may**, then **check with the speaker**, often privately, then **confirm in writing**. And the other way round: a Dutch *No, that won't work* is often the start of a discussion.

pairs.en: So when Pak Budi says 'we'll consider it', it may mean …
pairs.id: Jadi kalau Pak Budi bilang 'nanti kami pertimbangkan', mungkin maksudnya … (tafsirkan)

pairs.en: Could I check what you meant by …?
pairs.id: Boleh saya pastikan maksud Anda dengan …? (pastikan)

pairs.en: Just so I'm sure I've understood: …?
pairs.id: Supaya saya yakin sudah paham: …? (pastikan)

pairs.en: What would make this work for your team?
pairs.id: Apa yang bisa membuat ini cocok untuk timmu? (pertanyaan terbuka)

pairs.en: Just to confirm, … Is that right?
pairs.id: Sekadar konfirmasi, … Betul begitu? (tertulis)

steps.title: Your turn: the bridge sentence
steps.text: Kate has just heard a polite answer from the field coordinator. What do you tell her?

question.prompt: In Lombok, Kate proposes that field staff send daily reports on WhatsApp at 9 p.m. Pak Hendra, the coordinator, smiles and says 'Iya, Bu, nanti kami pertimbangkan.' The rest of the team stay quiet. Kate turns to you: 'Great, so they're on board?' What's the best reply?
options: Not necessarily. 'We'll consider it' can be a polite way of showing concerns here. Shall I ask Pak Hendra later what time would work for the team?
Yes, he said 'iya', so they'll start tonight.
No. People here never say what they really think.
question.explanation: The first reply interprets with a hedge (**can be**), doesn't guess for Pak Hendra, and proposes a private check. The second is the classic error: translating *iya, nanti kami pertimbangkan* as a firm yes. The third overclaims (it may not be a no) and is a stereotype (**never**).

steps.title: Reframe, and read the silence
steps.text: Two more bridging skills: changing the packaging, and hearing what silence means.
steps.body: **Reframing** = keep the **content**, change the **packaging**. Blunt → high-context listener: separate the message from the tone, give the context, add a next step. Indirect → direct listener: make the message explicit (*What Mr Sato is telling us, politely, is that the price is too high*). Never change the facts and never take sides. **Silence** in many Indonesian, Japanese and Thai meetings may mean thinking, respect or quiet disagreement, not agreement: ask by name, give time, follow up privately.

pairs.en: It isn't personal. Her main point is …
pairs.id: Ini bukan soal pribadi. Poin utamanya … (blak-blakan → halus)

pairs.en: What Mr Sato is telling us, politely, is …
pairs.id: Yang disampaikan Pak Sato, dengan sopan, adalah … (halus → jelas)

pairs.en: In this team, silence may mean people are still thinking.
pairs.id: Di tim ini, diam bisa berarti orang masih berpikir.

pairs.en: Rina, you know the field sites best. What do you think?
pairs.id: Rina, kamu yang paling tahu lokasinya. Bagaimana menurutmu? (sebut nama)

steps.title: Your turn: reframe the feedback
steps.text: A Dutch manager, an Indonesian analyst, and some very direct feedback.

question.prompt: In a team meeting in Jakarta, Anna, the Dutch manager, says about Sari's report: 'This analysis is weak. You need more data before we send it.' Afterwards, Sari tells you she's embarrassed. What's the best thing to say to her privately?
options: Anna thinks your report is bad. Don't take it personally.
In many Dutch workplaces, feedback like this is normal, and it's about the report, not you. Her main point is that the analysis needs more data. Shall we look at which figures to add?
Don't worry, Anna was only joking. The report is fine.
question.explanation: The second reply keeps the content (more data), gives the context (Dutch directness is normal), separates the work from the person and adds a next step. The first repeats the bluntness with no context. The third changes the facts: the problem will come back, bigger.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip each card. Say the English before you look.

many, often, tend to, in some workplaces
positive: showing closeness; negative: not imposing
Adapt the form, keep the content clear.

steps.title: Watch more
steps.text: Two short talks by Erin Meyer, author of The Culture Map: one on negative feedback across cultures, one on silence in meetings.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu jadi jembatan antarbudaya: kamu akan menjelaskan bagaimana orang cenderung bersikap dan kenapa, memilih kesopanan langsung atau tidak langsung untuk tiap pendengar, dan memastikan tidak ada yang mendengar 'nanti kami pertimbangkan' yang sopan sebagai ya yang pasti.

steps.title: Menjelaskan norma
steps.text: Di C1 kamu sudah menjelaskan konsep seperti sungkan, gotong royong, musyawarah dan jam karet dalam empat bagian. Sekarang kamu menjelaskan norma, ke dua arah.
steps.body: **Norma** adalah aturan tak tertulis tentang sikap: cara memanggil atasan, kapan menyampaikan kritik, apa yang ditanyakan ke rekan baru. Jelaskan dengan empat langkah: **kecenderungannya** (*In many Indonesian offices…*), **alasannya** (hormat, kerukunan, keakraban, efisiensi), **apa yang bukan maksudnya** (*It isn't rudeness*) dan **apa yang sebaiknya dilakukan** (*So it's a good idea to…*). Pakai **many / often / tend to**, jangan **always / all**, dan jangan pernah bilang satu budaya lebih baik.

steps.title: Giliranmu: jelaskan norma
steps.text: Sebuah LSM Australia di Lombok. Pilih penjelasan yang akan diberikan penengah yang baik.

question.prompt: Kate, direktur baru asal Australia di sebuah LSM di Lombok, bertanya kenapa separuh tim meninggalkan workshop hari Jumat pukul 11.30 dan kembali setelah pukul 13.00. Penjelasan mana yang terbaik?
options: Friday is a half day in Indonesia, so they're going home early.
Many Muslim men go to the mosque for Friday prayers around midday, so many workplaces here take a longer break. Lombok is mostly Muslim, so finish the morning session by 11.30.
People here aren't very serious about work on Fridays, so don't plan anything important.
question.explanation: Jawaban kedua menyebut kecenderungannya (**many** workplaces), alasannya (salat Jumat) dan apa yang sebaiknya dilakukan (selesai sebelum 11.30). Yang pertama faktanya salah: mereka kembali setelah pukul 13.00, jadi mereka tidak pulang. Yang ketiga mengubah praktik ibadah menjadi stereotip tentang malas.

steps.title: Kesopanan langsung dan tidak langsung
steps.text: Dua gagasan sederhana menjelaskan banyak kebingungan lintas budaya.
steps.body: **Low-context** (konteks rendah): pesannya sebagian besar ada di kata-kata. **High-context** (konteks tinggi): banyak pesan ada di hubungan dan yang tidak diucapkan. Kecenderungan umum: penutur Belanda, Jerman dan Australia lebih lugas; penutur Jepang, Thailand dan Indonesia lebih tidak langsung. **Kesopanan positif** = menunjukkan keakraban; **kesopanan negatif** = tidak memaksakan (*negatif* bukan berarti buruk). Pilih sesuai pendengar, hubungan, di depan umum atau empat mata, dan taruhannya: **sesuaikan bentuknya, isinya tetap jelas**.

steps.title: Giliranmu: pilih sesuai pendengar
steps.text: Klien Jepang dan kabar buruk soal pengiriman. Bentuk dan isi sama-sama penting.

question.prompt: Pak Sato, klien senior dari Jepang, sedang berkunjung ke pabrik di Cikarang. Kamu harus memberitahunya bahwa pengiriman pertama akan tiba terlambat lima hari. Pesan mana yang paling cocok untuknya?
options: Mr Sato, the shipment is late. It'll arrive on 20 March. That's all we can do.
We will do our best to send it soon, Mr Sato. Please don't worry.
Mr Sato, I'm very sorry. Because one machine broke down, the first shipment will arrive on 20 March, five days late. We've added a night shift so the next shipments stay on schedule.
question.explanation: Pesan ketiga menyesuaikan **bentuknya** untuk klien senior dari budaya konteks tinggi (permintaan maaf, alasan, rencana) dan **isinya** tetap jelas (tanggalnya, terlambat lima hari). Yang pertama jelas tapi blak-blakan, tanpa permintaan maaf. Yang kedua sopan tapi menyembunyikan keterlambatannya: salah paham yang mahal.

steps.title: Menjembatani makna: pahami, lalu pastikan
steps.text: Sekarang salah paham yang paling mahal di pelajaran ini.
steps.body: **Iya, nanti kami pertimbangkan** yang sopan bukan ya yang pasti: *iya* sering berarti *aku dengar*, dan *nanti kami pertimbangkan* bisa jadi **penolakan halus** (begitu juga *kami usahakan* dan *agak sulit, Pak*). Jangan terjemahkan kata per kata, tapi jangan juga mengubah setiap iya jadi tidak. **Tafsirkan dengan may**, lalu **pastikan ke pembicaranya**, sering kali empat mata, lalu **konfirmasi tertulis**. Dan sebaliknya: *No, that won't work* dari orang Belanda sering merupakan awal diskusi.

pairs.id: Jadi kalau Pak Budi bilang 'nanti kami pertimbangkan', mungkin maksudnya … (tafsirkan)

pairs.en: Could I check what you meant by …?
pairs.id: Boleh saya pastikan maksud Anda dengan …? (pastikan)

pairs.en: Just so I'm sure I've understood: …?
pairs.id: Supaya saya yakin sudah paham: …? (pastikan)

pairs.en: What would make this work for your team?
pairs.id: Apa yang bisa membuat ini cocok untuk timmu? (pertanyaan terbuka)

pairs.en: Just to confirm, … Is that right?
pairs.id: Sekadar konfirmasi, … Betul begitu? (tertulis)

steps.title: Giliranmu: kalimat jembatan
steps.text: Kate baru saja mendengar jawaban sopan dari koordinator lapangan. Apa yang kamu katakan padanya?

question.prompt: Di Lombok, Kate mengusulkan agar staf lapangan mengirim laporan harian lewat WhatsApp pukul 21.00. Pak Hendra, koordinatornya, tersenyum dan berkata 'Iya, Bu, nanti kami pertimbangkan.' Anggota tim lainnya diam. Kate menoleh padamu: 'Great, so they're on board?' Jawaban mana yang terbaik?
options: Not necessarily. 'We'll consider it' can be a polite way of showing concerns here. Shall I ask Pak Hendra later what time would work for the team?
Yes, he said 'iya', so they'll start tonight.
No. People here never say what they really think.
question.explanation: Jawaban pertama menafsirkan dengan hati-hati (**can be**), tidak menebak-nebak untuk Pak Hendra, dan mengusulkan untuk memastikan empat mata. Yang kedua kesalahan klasik: menerjemahkan *iya, nanti kami pertimbangkan* sebagai ya yang pasti. Yang ketiga berlebihan (belum tentu itu penolakan) dan stereotip (**never**).

steps.title: Bingkai ulang, dan baca diamnya
steps.text: Dua keterampilan menjembatani lagi: mengganti kemasan, dan memahami arti diam.
steps.body: **Membingkai ulang** = **isinya** tetap, **kemasannya** diganti. Blak-blakan → pendengar konteks tinggi: pisahkan pesan dari nadanya, beri konteks, tambahkan langkah berikutnya. Tidak langsung → pendengar lugas: jadikan pesannya jelas (*What Mr Sato is telling us, politely, is that the price is too high*). Jangan pernah mengubah fakta dan jangan memihak. **Diam** di banyak rapat di Indonesia, Jepang dan Thailand bisa berarti berpikir, hormat, atau tidak setuju diam-diam, bukan setuju: sebut nama, beri waktu, tindak lanjuti empat mata.

pairs.en: It isn't personal. Her main point is …
pairs.id: Ini bukan soal pribadi. Poin utamanya … (blak-blakan → halus)

pairs.en: What Mr Sato is telling us, politely, is …
pairs.id: Yang disampaikan Pak Sato, dengan sopan, adalah … (halus → jelas)

pairs.en: In this team, silence may mean people are still thinking.
pairs.id: Di tim ini, diam bisa berarti orang masih berpikir.

pairs.en: Rina, you know the field sites best. What do you think?
pairs.id: Rina, kamu yang paling tahu lokasinya. Bagaimana menurutmu? (sebut nama)

steps.title: Giliranmu: bingkai ulang masukannya
steps.text: Manajer asal Belanda, analis Indonesia, dan masukan yang sangat lugas.

question.prompt: Dalam rapat tim di Jakarta, Anna, manajer asal Belanda, berkata tentang laporan Sari: 'This analysis is weak. You need more data before we send it.' Sesudahnya Sari bilang padamu bahwa ia malu. Apa hal terbaik untuk kamu katakan kepadanya empat mata?
options: Anna thinks your report is bad. Don't take it personally.
In many Dutch workplaces, feedback like this is normal, and it's about the report, not you. Her main point is that the analysis needs more data. Shall we look at which figures to add?
Don't worry, Anna was only joking. The report is fine.
question.explanation: Jawaban kedua mempertahankan isinya (data tambahan), memberi konteks (lugas itu biasa di Belanda), memisahkan pekerjaan dari orangnya, dan menambahkan langkah berikutnya. Yang pertama mengulang kelugasannya tanpa konteks. Yang ketiga mengubah fakta: masalahnya akan kembali, lebih besar.

steps.text: Balik setiap kartu. Ucapkan bahasa Inggrisnya sebelum melihat.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Norma, strategi dan kalimat jembatan dalam satu halaman.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Mediasi lintas budaya
artifact.intro: Kecenderungan umum, bukan aturan tentang orang. Jelaskan, sesuaikan, pastikan.
rows: In many … offices, people … It's a way of showing … It isn't … So it's a good idea to …
kecenderungan + alasan + apa yang bukan + apa yang dilakukan
many / often / tend to / in some workplaces (bukan always / never / all)
kecenderungan, bukan label; tidak ada budaya yang lebih baik
Pak / Bu + nama depan (Pak Budi); Mr / Ms + nama belakang untuk kebanyakan orang Barat; nama depan di Australia dan Belanda
banyak orang Indonesia tidak punya nama keluarga
rapat kerja mulai tepat waktu; tenggat di Belanda atau Jerman itu janji: kabari dari awal
jam karet = hanya sebagian acara santai
kritik empat mata, pujian di depan umum (banyak lingkungan Indonesia, Jepang, Thailand)
usia, gaji, pernikahan, berat badan: ramah di Indonesia, sensitif di banyak tempat kerja Barat
usia membantu memilih Mbak, Kak, Bu, Dik
salat Jumat sekitar tengah hari; puasa Ramadan dari subuh sampai matahari terbenam; makanan halal saat menjamu
oleh-oleh / omiyage; sering dibuka belakangan; tangan kanan, atau dua tangan untuk hormat
Belanda, Jerman, Australia vs Jepang, Thailand, Indonesia (kecenderungan)
keakraban (nama depan, we) / tidak memaksakan (Could you possibly …?)
So when Pak Budi says 'we'll consider it', it may mean … / Could I check what you meant by …?
nanti kami pertimbangkan ≠ ya yang pasti
It isn't personal. Her main point is … / What Mr Sato is telling us, politely, is …
Silence may mean thinking or respect, not agreement. Ask by name.
tips: Sesuaikan bentuknya, isinya tetap jelas: keselamatan, uang dan tenggat butuh isi yang jelas untuk siapa pun.
Jangan terjemahkan 'iya, nanti kami pertimbangkan' menjadi 'yes, we agree'. Pakai 'may', lalu pastikan empat mata.
Penengah tidak mengubah fakta dan tidak memihak.

examples.en: In many Dutch workplaces, disagreeing openly with your manager is normal. It isn't a personal attack.
examples.id: Di banyak tempat kerja di Belanda, membantah manajer secara terbuka itu biasa. Itu bukan serangan pribadi.

examples.en: I'm sorry to trouble you, but would it be possible to add a little more data?
examples.id: Maaf merepotkan, tapi apakah mungkin datanya ditambah sedikit?

examples.en: What would make the new schedule work for your team?
examples.id: Apa yang bisa membuat jadwal baru ini cocok untuk timmu?

examples.en: In this team, silence may mean people are still thinking, not that they agree.
examples.id: Di tim ini, diam bisa berarti orang masih berpikir, bukan berarti setuju.
